local_checks.invariant: No job runs lower-trust (fork or branch pull request) code together with a secret, a write-capable token, an environment or deployment authority
local_checks.result: Triggers are only pull_request and push to develop/main (ci.yml:7-10). There is no pull_request_target, workflow_run, issue_comment, schedule or workflow_dispatch trigger. Top-level permissions is contents: read (ci.yml:13-14) and no job widens it (no id-token, packages, actions or contents write). grep for 'secrets.' and 'environment:' in the workflow and the composite action returns nothing. All six actions/checkout steps set persist-credentials: false. There is no publish, release, deploy or registry-push job in the repo, so no release boundary exists in source. The only privileged-looking value is SMEM_DEV_FIXED_OTP=123123 (ci.yml:235), set on one step of the e2e job, where the API runs with SMEM_ENV=test; it is a public, registered dev shortcut, not a credential. The CI service passwords (ci-only-fake-root-pw, ci-only-minio, ci-only-fake-minio-pw) are labelled throwaway, bound to 127.0.0.1 on an ephemeral runner, and protect no real data.

local_checks.invariant: Attacker-influenced values (branch name, PR text, go.mod content, go.dev response) do not reach a shell command, GITHUB_ENV or GITHUB_OUTPUT without validation
local_checks.result: Every ${{ }} in the workflow is enumerated (ci.yml:20,21,37,42,89,94,166,171,227,263,310,315 and action.yml:16): none is inside a run: block and none uses github.event.*, head_ref, a title or a body. steps.gover.outputs.minor (derived by awk from the PR's go.mod) is used only in with: inputs. The composite action receives it through env MINOR (action.yml:15-16), requires MINOR =~ ^1\.[0-9]+$ and the selected version =~ ^go<MINOR>\.[0-9]+$ before writing GOTOOLCHAIN to GITHUB_ENV (action.yml:28-30), so no newline or option injection is possible. A go.mod with several 'go' lines could add extra step outputs, but that happens only in the PR's own unprivileged run, which already controls the whole workflow file, so no boundary is crossed. Failure policy: on a go.dev outage or malformed JSON the step warns and keeps the setup-go toolchain (fail to a known source, not to an unverified one). When it does select a version, the go command downloads and verifies that toolchain against the Go checksum database, so a go.dev answer chooses only a version number and never supplies bytes. scripts/test-go-newest-patch.sh tests malformed answers and an injected MINOR.

local_checks.invariant: A lower-trust job cannot populate a cache or artifact that a higher-trust job restores, executes or releases
local_checks.result: There is no higher-trust job. The caches are setup-go (go.sum key), actions/cache for ~/.cache/ms-playwright (key playwright-<os>-<hash of tools/e2e/package-lock.json>) and the Trivy database (key trivy-db-<UTC date>, restore-keys trivy-db-). They are consumed only by the same workflow's test jobs with no secrets, and GitHub scopes caches written by a pull_request run to that PR's ref, so push runs on develop/main cannot restore them (hosted-runner default, not in source). Artifacts are write-only uploads on failure (e2e-failure, 3-day retention) or always (image-sbom, 30 days); no job downloads an artifact (grep: no download-artifact). The e2e artifact holds throwaway tokens and cookies only. The image job builds the production image but pushes nothing (docker build, no registry login).

local_checks.invariant: Helper scripts and Make targets run by CI do not widen runner authority (privileged containers, docker socket, secrets) and security gates fail closed

hardening_notes: SMEM_ENV is not required: internal/config/config.go:116 turns an unset or empty value into dev and the Dockerfile sets no ENV SMEM_ENV. A task definition that omits it boots with the dev posture (public constant OTP and cursor key when SMEM_OTP_KEY is unset, log mailer printing codes, non-Secure session cookie, no DB/Redis/S3 TLS requirement, unrestricted metrics bind), and cmd/smemories-migrate/main.go:43 would accept 'down --allow-down' against the production database. docs/production-config.md marks SMEM_ENV 'required, must be prod' but the loader does not enforce it. Fix: set ENV SMEM_ENV=prod in the Dockerfile (compose, e2e and the smoke test already set dev or test explicitly) or refuse an unset SMEM_ENV in the API, migrate and backfill binaries. Regression test: Load with SMEM_ENV unset returns an error.

internal/config/prod.go:45-53 checks only mc.TLSConfig == 'true' for the production DSN. A DSN with tls=true&allowFallbackToPlaintext=true (or the same parameter together with SMEM_DB_TLS_CA_FILE, which skips the DSN parse) would, from my recollection of the go-sql-driver handshake and unverified offline because no module cache exists, let a network attacker who strips the server's TLS capability force plaintext. The DSN is operator-controlled, so this is hardening: reject mc.AllowFallbackToPlaintext in prod.

local_checks.invariant: Every cookie-authenticated state-changing route (POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE) refuses a request whose Origin (or Referer when Origin is absent) is not in the SMEM_ALLOWED_ORIGINS allowlist whenever the smem_session cookie is sent, and refuses bodies that are not application/json (multipart/form-data on the upload route).
local_checks.result: Inventory of all mux registrations (main.go:180 wires authH, bookH, mediaH, notesH, bookDataH, templateH, feedbackH). All 20 POST routes are wrapped in auth.Guard or auth.GuardMultipart except POST /api/public-collect/submit-note (notes/handler.go:68), which never calls RequireUser/MustUser and is cookie-less by design (link token is the credential). All GET routes (get-me, lists, get-content, book-data, template list, google-start/callback, healthz, readyz) change no account state. Guard runs outside RequireUser on every route (csrf.go:36-48, handler.go:42-43, notes/handler.go:58, yearbook/handler.go:29, media/handler.go:61,65). The cookie-presence test (csrf.go:39) uses r.Cookie(CookieName), the same parser cookieToken (handler.go:283) uses, so there is no parse divergence between 'cookie present' and 'session resolved'. requestOrigin (csrf.go:54-64) rejects Origin 'null', unparsable values, userinfo and suffix tricks; a bad Origin is never rescued by a good Referer. Content-Type is enforced for any ContentLength != 0 (chunked is -1, so also covered). No CORS headers, no OPTIONS route, no method-override header or _method handling exists (grep), so cross-origin JSON cannot pass a preflight. Cookie-less login/register CSRF is blocked by the Content-Type rule because a cross-site form cannot send application/json. SameSite=Lax (handler.go:298) means the cookie is not sent on cross-site POST anyway. No accepted cross-site state change found.

local_checks.invariant: Host, Forwarded and X-Forwarded-* metadata do not decide absolute URLs, callbacks, reset links or authorization; the client address used by limiters comes from RemoteAddr unless SMEM_TRUST_PROXY is explicitly on, and then only from the last hop appended by the proxy.
local_checks.result: ResolveClientIP (middleware.go:238-252) reads only X-Forwarded-For, only when trustProxy is true, takes the last header line and its last comma-separated hop, and requires net.ParseIP to accept it, else falls back to the RemoteAddr host. The same setting reaches WithClientIP (router.go:40, main.go:180) and auth.Handler.clientIP (handler.go:306, main.go:135), so there is one policy. No code reads r.Host, X-Forwarded-Host/Proto, Forwarded or X-Real-IP (grep). The Google redirect URL and email content come from SMEM_PUBLIC_BASE_URL or stored data, not the request (main.go:141); the code emails contain a 6-digit code and no link (en.tmpl, mail.go). Residual risk is deployment only: with TrustProxy=true on a task clients can reach directly, X-Forwarded-For is forgeable and per-IP limits can be walked around; with false behind an ALB all clients share one bucket. docs/production-config.md:117-122 documents exactly this; the repo has no ingress source to confirm the real setting.

local_checks.invariant: No untrusted value reaches Location, Set-Cookie, Retry-After, Allow or any other response header with control characters.
local_checks.result: Header sinks in my paths: X-Request-Id echoes only values matching ^[A-Za-z0-9-]{8,64}$ (Go RE2 '$' is end-of-text, so a trailing newline fails) else a random hex id (middleware.go:42,59-68); Retry-After values are integers computed from durations (handler.go:250-268); Set-Cookie carries a base64url random token or an empty value (handler.go:296-299); Allow is copied from the mux's own 405 (router.go:70); SecurityHeaders sets constants (middleware.go:144-153). The Location writes in google.go are owned by the peer OIDC unit; I only confirmed they are constants or safeReturnTo output (relative paths, control characters rejected). No response-header injection reachable from this unit.

hardening_notes: Session cookie smem_session has no __Host- prefix (handler.go:296-299); a less-trusted sibling subdomain could toss a Domain-scoped cookie of the same name into a logged-out browser (acts as session fixation toward the attacker's account). Deployment dependent; renaming to __Host-smem_session (Secure, Path=/, no Domain) closes it.

Sessions slide for 30 days with no absolute lifetime and the sliding refresh re-sends the same token (service.go:288-297); there is no sign-out-everywhere endpoint other than password reset. Consider an absolute cap and token rotation on refresh.

Account recovery can be denied by an anonymous caller who knows the address: forgot_email allows only 3 codes per hour per address regardless of caller (service.go:34, reset.go:22), and 5 wrong guesses lock the live reset code (codes.go:71,80), so repeated attacker requests can keep a victim from resetting. Consider counting limits per (address, IP) or letting the owner of the mailbox bypass.

Verification-code guess budget for an unverified squatter account is about 15 tries per hour sustained (3 resends x 5 tries, verify_tries 20/h), roughly 1% per month, while the victim mailbox receives 3 mails per hour. A verified squatter account would be linked as a 'verified local account' by the Google flow without stripping its password or sessions (store.go:256), so adding a cumulative cap or daily lock after N failures would harden the pre-hijack defence.

Login, register, forgot and reset routes (no cookie) are protected from cross-site POST only by the application/json Content-Type rule and the absence of CORS; keep the invariant that any route outside auth.Guard (submit-note, lookup) must never read the session cookie or call RequireUser.

SecureCookie is derived from cfg.Env != dev and Env defaults to dev (config.go:116); a production task that omits SMEM_ENV would also select the log mailer, public OTP key and non-Secure cookie. Owned by the peer SMEM_ENV precedence unit; consider failing start-up when SMEM_PUBLIC_BASE_URL is https but Env is dev.

TrustProxy is not enforced or warned about in prod config (prod.go has no rule); a wrong value either shares one limiter bucket across all clients (false behind an ALB) or lets clients forge their address (true on a directly reachable task). docs/production-config.md:117-122 documents the requirement; a start-up warning when trust is on and the peer address is not private would help.

local_checks.result: SMEM_OTP_KEY is at least 32 bytes, or the public constant devOTPKey only when SMEM_ENV is dev or test (config.go:83, 353-363). codes.go:125-129 HMACs 'purpose|uid|code' with the raw key. cursor.go:25-28 derives the AES-256 key as HMAC(key, 'smemories/cursor/v1'). The OIDC cookie uses the separate SMEM_OIDC_COOKIE_KEY (google.go:136-140, config.go:431-438). The three message spaces cannot collide even if an operator reuses one value: code inputs start with verify| or reset| and contain '|', the cursor label contains '/', and cookie payloads are base64url, which has neither. No endpoint returns HMAC(OTPKey, chosen input) to a client, so key reuse is not exploitable. Hardening only: the codes key is not label-derived and equal OIDC/OTP keys are not rejected.

Refund is ZPOPMAX of the newest member (redis.go:51): it may pop another request's hit under concurrency but the net hit count stays correct, so Take+Refund is count-neutral (checked against the consumers in notes/service.go, media/service.go and, read only for refund semantics, auth Login/UpdateUsername/ResendVerification: no bypass). Names are fixed constants so smem:<env>:rl:<name>:<key> cannot collide across limiters. guard.Take fails open for Open limiters and returns ErrUnavailable for Closed ones, logs at most one ERROR per minute, and treats context.Canceled as neither (redis.go:136-155). Per-IP keys are whatever raw string the caller passes (hardening note below).

local_checks.invariant: Public-route and submission limits are charged once per request, refunded only when the server turned the request away, and the per-link note cap, active-link cap, deadline and revocation hold under concurrency; per-owner counts of links and notes are bounded
local_checks.result: Resolve takes public_all then public_misses per IP and refunds misses only when the error is not NotFound (service.go:161-184). SubmitNote validates text before charging the three submission limiters, takeSubmit refunds partial takes (service.go:300-315), and all four counters are refunded only for media.ErrBusy (service.go:242-247); invalid images, quota and full-link answers stay charged. insertNote re-reads revoked_at, deadline and the 300-note count under the collection row lock after the yearbook share lock (store.go:202-245); create enforces maxActive=5 under the yearbook FOR UPDATE lock (store.go:40-67). Moderation writes are limited to 120 per minute per user after cheap validation (moderation.go:158-164). Gap found: the active-link cap counts only non-revoked rows (store.go:55), revoke is a soft delete with no purge endpoint (handler.go:59-65), create/revoke have no limiter (service.go:110-157) and get-list returns every row without a LIMIT (store.go:79-81), so per-owner link and note growth is unbounded; reported as candidate notes.collection.unbounded-revoked-rows-unpaged-list (needs_validation).

local_checks.invariant: The per-user yearbook cap is enforced atomically, ownership scoping is applied before any state change, and inputs have numeric bounds
local_checks.result: Create locks the user_tab row and counts yearbooks before inserting, so concurrent creates cannot exceed 20 (store.go:203-235; maxBooksOwned in validate.go:29). Every get/list/modify/remove query carries owner_id; media and cover references are checked to belong to the same book under a share lock (store.go:357-370). Field limits and year/birthday bounds are validated in validate.go. Service.Delete purges objects first and then removes rows in one transaction (service.go:122-133); the id spelling used for the purge and the orphan race are owned by the peer lifecycle unit and not duplicated here.

hardening_notes: Media quota counts only len(p.display) (internal/media/service.go:150) while the print and thumb objects are stored too (service.go:152-162); for photos of 1800 px or less the print object duplicates the display bytes, so real S3 use per user can reach roughly 2x the 500 MiB constant (store.go:15) plus thumbnails. Count all stored bytes or document the factor.

save() pre-checks the quota with add=0 (internal/media/service.go:121), so when the owner is within one photo of the 500 MiB limit every upload is fully decoded, re-encoded, written as 3 objects and deleted again before ErrQuota at store.go:103; pass an upper bound for the new size to the pre-check.

The processing-slot release is a plain statement, not a defer (internal/media/service.go:137-143): a panic inside load() or process() is caught by the Recover middleware but leaks a slot permanently (default 2 slots), after which owner uploads wait forever and contributor uploads return ERROR_BUSY until restart. Use defer or recover around the slot section.

Contributor photos share the owner's 200-photo / 500 MiB quota with no per-link or reserved owner budget (internal/media/service.go:115, store.go:75): one holder of a widely shared link can fill a yearbook's 200 photos in about 67 submissions (60 per hour per link) and block the owner's own uploads and other friends' photos with ERROR_QUOTA_EXCEEDED until the owner deletes notes or revokes the link. Consider a per-link photo cap or a reserved owner allowance.

notes.SubmitNote refunds all four counters on ErrBusy even when earlier photos of the same request were already decoded, stored and then discarded (internal/notes/service.go:242-248); refund only when no photo was processed, otherwise a request can cost S3 and DB work without being counted.

Rate-limit keys for IP budgets are the raw address string from httpx.ResolveClientIP (internal/httpx/middleware.go:247-251, used at notes/service.go:162 and by the auth limiters): an attacker with an IPv6 prefix gets a fresh budget per address. Group IPv6 by /64 before keying. The largest effect is on register/login limiters owned by peer units; within the notes routes the per-collection limit and the 300-note cap still hold.

The public submission path has no CAPTCHA (notes/verifier.go:15-17 allowAll, handler.go:43) and a filled honeypot field returns success after the body was spooled without taking any submit limiter (notes/submit.go:124-127), so only public_all (600 per 15 min per IP) and the connection slots bound that path.

smemories-migrate refuses down only when SMEM_ENV=prod (cmd/smemories-migrate/main.go:43), SMEM_ENV defaults to dev (internal/config/config.go:116) and the Dockerfile sets no ENV, so a one-off task run against the production DSN without SMEM_ENV=prod can execute destructive down migrations. Tie the refusal to the target (for example a marker row in app_meta) or require an explicit ALLOW flag in addition.

Dev-selected behaviours are neither tagged DEV-SHORTCUT nor registered in docs/dev-shortcuts.md: the public devOTPKey fallback for SMEM_OTP_KEY (config.go:83,359-361; it also keys the cursor tokens), the log mailer, Secure=false cookies when SMEM_ENV=dev (main.go:135) and localhost defaults for origins and base URL. They are safe only because prod refuses them, and the planned scripts/check-no-dev-shortcuts.sh (does not exist yet) will not see them; the four *_ALLOW_INSECURE opt-outs (prod.go:20-34) are likewise unregistered transport weakeners.
.gitignore does not cover .env.development, .env.test, .env.*.local, *.p12, *.pfx, *.tfvars, terraform state or credentials.json; only .env.example is tracked today.

.claude/settings.json pre-approves Bash(make *), go run, npm install and git push for any Claude Code session opened in the repo, so build files from an untrusted branch execute without a prompt; developer-environment risk only.
design/canvas/temp1-8.html (about 15 MB of compressed design bundles with scripts) is tracked but is not part of the image or the web build; remove it from the public repo or document its origin.
API responses carry no Strict-Transport-Security or Content-Security-Policy header (internal/httpx/middleware.go:144-153); this is fine only if the edge adds them, which is outside the repository.

ratelimit.Redis.Refund pops the newest hit of the key, not the caller's own (internal/ratelimit/redis.go:51); counts stay correct, but a lost or duplicated Refund after a Redis error shifts the budget by one, so keep fail-closed limiters free of refund paths that run after a failed Take.

local_checks.invariant: Only an email-verified owner can create collection links and read/moderate notes; the verified flag cannot be stale or spoofed from the request.
local_checks.result: Every note route is wrapped in requireUser (POST routes also in auth.Guard). CreateCollection (service.go:111) and ListNotes/UpdateStatus/ReorderNotes/DeleteNotes/ApprovedNotes all call the verified check (checkOwner, moderation.go:108) with u.EmailVerified. That value comes from auth.Service.Authenticate, which re-reads user_tab (email_verified_at IS NOT NULL) on every request (service.go:281, store.go:57), so there is no cached or session-borne flag. No code path clears email_verified_at (only markEmailVerified and the Google-link path set it). Collection list and revoke skip the verified check, but they are owner-scoped and only touch links that needed a verified owner to create. Request bodies use DisallowUnknownFields and never carry owner_id; the owner id comes only from the session user.

local_checks.invariant: Every read and write of collections, notes and note photos is bound to the authenticated owner's yearbook; a foreign or missing id fails the same way.
local_checks.result: create, list, ownedBook, lockOwnedBook and approvedPage all filter yearbook_tab by owner_id AND public_id. revoke joins yearbook_tab on owner_id. lockNotes, noteRowIDs, setStatus, reorder and removeNotes all bind note_tab.yearbook_id to the locked, owner-checked book id, and any id outside it returns ErrNotFound for the whole batch (no partial effect, no foreign/missing difference). fillNotes and mediaOf only follow note ids already scoped to the book. checkIDs/isPublicID force canonical upper-case Crockford ULIDs and reject duplicates, which closes the case-insensitive/accent-insensitive utf8mb4_0900_ai_ci spelling gap that the collation would otherwise allow. ulid.New emits upper-case, so the stored form always matches the canonical check. Every IN list is guarded against n=0 (withIn would panic), and all call sites require non-empty ids.

local_checks.invariant: Moderation transitions (pending/approved/hidden, reorder, delete) and the public insert cannot reach an invalid state or slip past revoke, deadline or cap checks under concurrency.
local_checks.result: Lock order is yearbook_tab (FOR UPDATE for moderation and create, FOR SHARE for public insert and revoke), then collection or note rows. insertNote re-reads revoked_at, deadline_at and the note count under the collection FOR UPDATE, so a revoked link or a full link stores nothing and the caller discards its photos. setStatus is all-or-nothing, approves by appending after MAX(sort_order), and renumbers when notes leave the approved set. reorder demands exactly the approved set, otherwise ERROR_ORDER_STALE. Any status can move to any other status; no transition grants anything beyond the owner's own book, so there is no state-machine escalation. place() argument order matches its SQL placeholders. Residual low-impact timing: the deadline compare in insertNote uses the submission-start timestamp (hardening note).

local_checks.invariant: Contributor photos attached to notes belong to the same yearbook and owner as the note, and media row access is owner-scoped.
local_checks.result: SubmitNote calls UploadContributorFrom with p.YearbookID, which comes from the token-hash lookup, and the owner id is derived from yearbook_tab by row id (yearbookByRow), never from a request field. media.insert re-checks yearbook_tab id AND owner_id FOR SHARE and enforces quota under a user-row lock. store.owned and list are scoped by owner or by an owner-checked yearbook id. Note photos therefore always point at media rows in the note's own book.

local_checks.invariant: Owner-side collection endpoints never expose the link token after creation, and only the SHA-256 is stored.
local_checks.result: newToken returns the token once (createdCollection in the create response); Collection and collectionJSON carry no token or hash. The list query selects public_id, label, deadline_at, created_at, revoked_at and a note count only. The token_hash column is unique.

local_checks.invariant: The schema does not undermine the app-level owner scoping or note-to-photo uniqueness.
local_checks.result: public_id columns are CHAR(26) UNIQUE with utf8mb4_0900_ai_ci (case- and accent-insensitive), which is why the canonical-ULID check is needed; the notes routes enforce it. note_photo_tab keeps a unique media_id, so a photo belongs to exactly one note. After the _tab conversions there are no foreign keys, so cascade is application-level (deleteByYearbook, deleteMediaLinks), covered under the deletion unit.

hardening_notes: internal/yearbook/service.go:128 passes the request's id string to PurgeYearbook instead of the DB-canonical y.ID, and internal/media/service.go:89-97,149 builds the S3 key from the typed yearbook_id. Return the stored public_id from ownedYearbook and use it for keys and purge. Also require canonical upper-case ULIDs on yearbook, media and note-collection routes, as the notes moderation routes already do with isPublicID. Regression test: upload with a lower-case yearbook_id, delete the book, assert no object under any spelling remains.

internal/media/service.go:328 documents that an upload or submission racing a yearbook delete can leave orphan objects. A second DeletePrefix after Store.remove commits would close it: once the book is gone, any in-flight insert fails and its own cleanup runs, so objects written before the commit are the only leftovers.

internal/media/store.go:155-160 (Media.keys) omits the print object when print_key is empty, but the key is deterministic (printKey(ObjectKey)). Always including it closes the interleaving in internal/media/backfill.go:85-95 where setPrintKey succeeds after Delete read an empty PrintKey, leaving a 1800 px copy of a deleted photo until the yearbook purge.

internal/media/service.go:286 (DeleteObjects) and :307 (DeleteRows) accept raw media row ids with no owner or yearbook parameter. They are safe today only because notes.Service passes ids from owner-scoped queries; consider taking the owner-checked yearbook id and filtering by it so a future caller cannot delete another tenant's photo.

internal/notes/service.go:225,267 and internal/notes/store.go:219 compare the deadline against the submission start time, but photo processing can take up to roughly a minute, so a submission started just before the deadline can commit after it. Use the commit-time clock if the cutoff must be exact.

POST /api/note-collection/create has no per-user limiter, and only non-revoked rows count toward maxActive (internal/notes/store.go:55), so a verified owner can create and revoke links without bound and grow note_collection_tab. This only affects the owner's own data growth.

internal/storage/s3.go deletes with plain DeleteObjects and no version id. If the production bucket is versioned, this only adds delete markers and old versions stay until a lifecycle rule expires them. Nothing in the repo shows the bucket configuration, so confirm noncurrent-version expiry matches the deletion promise.

The notes next_id scope (note/get-list:<book>:<status>) does not include the owner id although docs/moderation.md describes it as user-bound. It is equivalent today because a book has exactly one owner and the query is also owner-scoped; keep it that way if sharing or transfer is ever added.

local_checks.invariant: A link token authorizes exactly one active collection, is unguessable, is stored only as a hash, and unknown, malformed and revoked tokens are indistinguishable to a caller who does not hold a live token.
local_checks.result: Tokens are 24 crypto/rand bytes, base64url, 32 chars (token.go:10-20); tokenHash rejects anything of the wrong length or alphabet before the database and returns SHA-256 (token.go:24-35). The column is BINARY(32) with a unique index (0008_note_collections.sql), so the comparison is exact and case-sensitive. Store.lookup (store.go:160-176) selects by token_hash AND revoked_at IS NULL and returns ErrNotFound for no row; Service.Resolve (service.go:161-184) maps malformed, unknown and revoked to the same ErrNotFound (404, same message) and returns the distinct 410 ErrClosed only for an active token past its deadline, which only a holder can reach. The token resolves to collection id and yearbook id only; lookup returns yearbook title, owner display_name, deadline and the form's field descriptors, with no collection label, no note data and no other collection. The plaintext token is returned once by create (handler.go:92,113) and list omits it. Per-IP limiters (public_all 600, public_misses 60 per 15 min) bound guessing against a 192-bit space. Refund pops the newest hit, but each Take/Refund pair is net zero, so the miss counter cannot be reduced by interleaving. No invariant failure found.

local_checks.invariant: The query-string bearer token is not written to server logs, errors, metrics, caches, Referer headers, third-party origins or persistent browser storage by anything in the repository.
local_checks.result: Routes are registered without CORS and without cookies (handler.go:66-68); the token is read with r.URL.Query().Get('token') in lookup and submit and passed to Resolve only. AccessLog records the mux pattern, never the query (middleware.go:97-117); notes errors never embed the token (handler.go:176-190 and the service return static messages). Every API response carries Cache-Control: no-store (middleware.go:150). web/index.html sets a no-referrer meta, NoteForm adds noindex and no-referrer metas on mount, and no analytics, error-reporting or service-worker code exists in web/src (grep). The draft key in localStorage is a 53-bit hash of the token, not the token (NoteForm.tsx:57-79), and NoteLinks/notes.ts keep the plaintext token only in component state. Fonts are self-hosted (fontsource), so the /c/:token page loads no third-party origin. The token also appears in the SPA page URL (/c/:token), so any edge or ALB access log that records URLs sees it regardless of how the API call carries it; that is a deployment fact outside the repository and is recorded as hardening, not a candidate.

local_checks.invariant: The public lookup discloses only data the owner chose to share with a link holder and provides no existence, state or timing oracle for non-holders; the abuse verifier and limiters behave as the design states.
local_checks.result: Non-holders get one 404 for every non-live token. The two limiters run before the DB lookup; a malformed token skips the database, which reveals only the token format. The disclosed owner display_name is the registered or Google name; when Google gives no usable name, SignInGoogle falls back to the email local part (google.go:333-339), so a link holder can see an email local part for such accounts: low-impact data minimisation note, not a boundary failure because the holder is the owner's intended audience. The CAPTCHA verifier is allowAll (verifier.go:17), so abuse resistance on submit rests on limiters and the honeypot, which is a peer unit's concern. No invariant failure found.

hardening_notes: The link token travels in the query string (GET /api/public-collect/get, POST submit-note) and also in the SPA path /c/:token. App logs omit it, but any ALB or CloudFront access log that records URLs would capture it whatever the API transport. When T-023 lands, disable or restrict URL logging for /c/* and /api/public-collect/*, or move the token to the URL fragment plus a header or body field.
Add X-Robots-Tag: noindex at the edge for /c/*; the noindex meta is injected by JavaScript only after load (NoteForm.tsx).

GET /readyz and /healthz are unauthenticated and /readyz takes a pooled DB connection and does a Redis SET per request with no limiter. Keep /readyz off the public listener or cache its result for about a second.

SMEM_METRICS_ALLOW_ANY_INTERFACE=true binds the unauthenticated metrics listener to every interface. The only control is a security group that is not in the repository, so verify the metrics port is absent from the ALB target group and from public security-group rules.

LogMailer prints codes to the same stdout stream as the JSON app log; this is safe only because NewLog and loadMail refuse non-dev/test and non-ses prod. SMEM_ENV=test is accepted by config and also gets the public dev OTP key; make sure no deployed environment uses dev or test.
Print-feedback counters can be skewed at 30 per IP per hour and have no consumer in code. If the numbers ever drive a decision, treat them as untrusted telemetry.
Google sign-in falls back to the email local part as display_name (google.go:333-339), which the public link lookup returns to link holders. Prefer a neutral default such as 'Student'.

NoteForm persists text drafts in localStorage keyed by a token hash on the device until the note is sent. On a shared computer a later visitor opening the same link sees the earlier draft; consider sessionStorage.

local_checks.invariant: One principal cannot hold more than its per-IP share of the 48 global public-submission slots, and a request that is rejected (rate limited, unknown token) does not keep a slot longer than the work it costs.
local_checks.result: acquire/release are correct and panic-safe (submit.go:59-63, 238-264; counters under one mutex, map entry deleted at zero). The per-IP dimension is the raw address string: ResolveClientIP returns the host verbatim (middleware.go:238-252, v2_test.go:312) and the limiter keys are the same string (notes/service.go:162-167, ratelimit/redis.go:181), so an IPv6 /64 (or 6 IPv4 addresses) reaches the 48-slot cap. Only NotFound is answered without reading the body (submit.go:73-76); a RateLimited answer goes through drainWriter and keeps the slot until the body is drained, up to the 120 s pace limit (submit.go:69, 290-307, httpx/respond.go:73-83), so the earlier limiters do not protect the slots. Candidate notes/submit-slot-cap-raw-ip-key-and-drain-on-reject (needs_validation: IPv6 exposure, WAF).

local_checks.invariant: Spooled bytes on disk are bounded by real capacity: connections x 32 MiB never exceeds the spool volume, and spool files are always removed.
local_checks.result: Cleanup is sound: CreateTemp is followed at once by a deferred Close+Remove (submit.go:99-107, also on panic), SweepSpool removes aged orphans only for regular smem-upload-* files (spool.go:32-59). Capacity is not tied to the caps: worst case is SMEM_PUBLIC_UPLOAD_MAX_CONNS x maxBody = 48 x 32 MiB (handler.go:19, submit.go:20) but CheckSpool only creates and removes one empty file (spool.go:18-26, main.go:174), config only checks the directory exists, and docs/container.md:23 shows a 64 MiB tmpfs. A full spool turns into 500s for everyone (submit.go:108-114). Candidate notes/submit-spool-capacity-not-tied-to-slot-cap (needs_validation: production volume type/size).

local_checks.invariant: A slow or stalled public body is dropped on a bounded schedule and the spooled structure is parsed with bounded work.
local_checks.result: Covered. PaceBody resets the read deadline to min(now+10 s, start+120 s) before every read and fails the read below 16 KiB/s average after 15 s (respond.go:73-83); the 32 MiB cap is a route-level MaxBytesReader replacing the 1 MiB default (middleware.go:190-198, handler.go:68). scan reads at most 12 parts, 16 KiB answers, 1 KiB honeypot and counts photo parts without buffering (submit.go:178-234); loadPhoto re-reads the same spooled bytes with the same boundary and caps at maxPhoto+1 (submit.go:154-167). A credit trick (front-load about 2 MiB, then one byte per <10 s) holds a slot for at most the 120 s total, which is the bound used in the slot candidate.

local_checks.invariant: Photo processing for public submissions is slot-bounded, waits a bounded time, does not hold memory while queued, and cancelled or failed submissions delete what they stored.
local_checks.result: Covered. UploadContributorFrom calls the loader only after a processing slot is held and waits at most 10 s (media/service.go:110-143); SubmitNote validates text and rate limits before any photo work and Discards stored photos on every failure with its own context (notes/service.go:240-270, media/service.go:173-182). process is not cancellable but is bounded by the pixel limits. The CAPTCHA verifier is allowAll and runs after the body is spooled (hardening).

hardening_notes: internal/media/image.go:74-78: the print variant is scaled and encoded in a goroutine (wg.Go) with no recover; a panic there would terminate the whole process, not one request (the Recover middleware only covers the handler goroutine). No panic input was found; wrap the goroutine body in a recover that returns an error.
internal/media/service.go:137-142: release the processing slot with defer so a decoder panic cannot leak it (also see candidate media/process-header-dims-trust-and-sem-release-without-defer).

internal/media/image.go:200-222: decodedBytes undercounts two cases verified in the Go 1.26 stdlib: 4-component (CMYK/YCCK) JPEG allocates an extra 4 bytes per pixel in applyBlack (image/jpeg/reader.go:675-738) on top of the 2.5-4 counted, and Adam7-interlaced PNG allocates per-pass images on top of the full image (image/png/reader.go:375-390, up to about 1.5x). The worst cases stay near the already-measured 490 MB per slot in docs/media.md, but the 128 MiB estimate is not the true peak; add a factor for 4-component JPEG and interlaced PNG or re-measure.

internal/media/service.go:73,94: the 60-uploads-per-10-minutes limiter is per user id and gives no fairness on the 2 shared processing slots; a handful of free accounts (registration is limited per raw IP only) uploading 50 MP JPEGs of a few hundred KB can keep both slots busy and make owners wait and contributors get 503 after 10 s. A per-owner or per-IP concurrency cap on slots would bound it (limiter unit is owned by a peer).
internal/media/store.go:75 and service.go:150: quota counts only len(display) bytes, so thumbnail and print objects (roughly +30-50%) are uncounted storage (quota unit is owned by a peer).

internal/media/handler.go:268-287: HEAD, If-None-Match and Range requests on get-content still fetch the whole object from S3 before ETag/Range are evaluated; consider evaluating the ETag from the database row first.

internal/notes/submit.go:136-137 and verifier.go:17: the CAPTCHA hook runs after the 32 MiB body is spooled and the default verifier is allowAll, so even when wired it cannot gate disk or connection cost; run it before spooling or after Resolve for first-time IPs.
internal/notes/spool.go:18-26: CheckSpool could also check free space against SMEM_PUBLIC_UPLOAD_MAX_CONNS x maxBody and refuse to start (or lower the cap) when the spool is smaller.

hardening_notes: Media quota counts only len(p.display) (internal/media/service.go:150) while the print and thumb objects are stored too (service.go:152-162); for photos of 1800 px or less the print object duplicates the display bytes, so real S3 use per user can reach roughly 2x the 500 MiB constant (store.go:15) plus thumbnails. Count all stored bytes or document the factor.

save() pre-checks the quota with add=0 (internal/media/service.go:121), so when the owner is within one photo of the 500 MiB limit every upload is fully decoded, re-encoded, written as 3 objects and deleted again before ErrQuota at store.go:103; pass an upper bound for the new size to the pre-check.

The processing-slot release is a plain statement, not a defer (internal/media/service.go:137-143): a panic inside load() or process() is caught by the Recover middleware but leaks a slot permanently (default 2 slots), after which owner uploads wait forever and contributor uploads return ERROR_BUSY until restart. Use defer or recover around the slot section.

Contributor photos share the owner's 200-photo / 500 MiB quota with no per-link or reserved owner budget (internal/media/service.go:115, store.go:75): one holder of a widely shared link can fill a yearbook's 200 photos in about 67 submissions (60 per hour per link) and block the owner's own uploads and other friends' photos with ERROR_QUOTA_EXCEEDED until the owner deletes notes or revokes the link. Consider a per-link photo cap or a reserved owner allowance.

notes.SubmitNote refunds all four counters on ErrBusy even when earlier photos of the same request were already decoded, stored and then discarded (internal/notes/service.go:242-248); refund only when no photo was processed, otherwise a request can cost S3 and DB work without being counted.

Rate-limit keys for IP budgets are the raw address string from httpx.ResolveClientIP (internal/httpx/middleware.go:247-251, used at notes/service.go:162 and by the auth limiters): an attacker with an IPv6 prefix gets a fresh budget per address. Group IPv6 by /64 before keying. The largest effect is on register/login limiters owned by peer units; within the notes routes the per-collection limit and the 300-note cap still hold.

The public submission path has no CAPTCHA (notes/verifier.go:15-17 allowAll, handler.go:43) and a filled honeypot field returns success after the body was spooled without taking any submit limiter (notes/submit.go:124-127), so only public_all (600 per 15 min per IP) and the connection slots bound that path.

hardening_notes: The SPA is not served by the Go API and web/index.html carries no CSP or framing control; the API-only SecurityHeaders (internal/httpx/middleware.go:143-153) sets X-Frame-Options DENY on API responses only. Not a finding today: the session cookie is HttpOnly SameSite=Lax and is withheld from cross-site frames.

Registration lets anyone have a verification email sent to an arbitrary address with an attacker-chosen display name (up to 100 characters, URL-like text allowed) in the greeting (internal/auth/mail.go:81, emails/en.tmpl:2,7).
